subject: Shadow sessions spike on June invoice - request for logs and credit
messages:
From: Anna Lee <anna.lee@brightcart.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@brightcart.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:12:00 +0000
Subject: Unexpected jump on June invoice (INV-20260615)

Hi Evelyn,

We just received invoice INV-20260615 and we're seeing a ~38% increase in token consumption vs. our baseline for the month of June. The charge appears to be concentrated in multiple short-lived sessions around 2026-06-15 that we don't recognize.

Can you please:
- Share the per-request/session logs you have for 2026-06-14 through 2026-06-16 (token-level or at least request IDs + timestamps).
- Confirm whether any automatic reprocessing or replay jobs were run on our account from Redwood's side.
- Advise next steps for a credit if this turns out to be a billing-side duplication.

We've attached a small sample from our side (brightcart_usage_sample_20260615.csv). We are EU-based and will need any VAT adjustments documented for our finance team.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement needs the final amount for month-close.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Lee
Head of Finance, BrightCart
anna.lee@brightcart.com
+44 20 7946 0123

Attachment: brightcart_usage_sample_20260615.csv (CSV, 28KB)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lee <anna.lee@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected jump on June invoice (INV-20260615)

Anna — thanks for the heads up and the sample. We're pulling token-level traces now. Quick notes / ask:

- Can you confirm whether you performed any migration or changed an integration key around 2026-06-15 00:00-06:00 UTC? The pattern looks like many short-lived sessions from the same agent but different request IDs.
- I'll loop in Ben (billing) to help with a provisional credit if the anomaly is on our side; Marissa will handle the VAT paperwork.

Next steps:
1) Ben and I will review the token logs and surface any duplicate/echoed requests.
2) If we identify a server-side duplication, we'll propose a one-time adjustment for the overage (provisional) while we finalize evidence.
3) We'll provide an export of matching request IDs + timestamps and a short summary for your accounting team.

I'll share a first-pass log excerpt by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Lead, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai

On Thu, 18 Jun 2026 at 13:12, Anna Lee <anna.lee@brightcart.com> wrote:
> (original message quoted)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:24:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Unexpected jump on June invoice (INV-20260615)

Eve — quick diagnostic: pulled session traces for BrightCart across 2026-06-14..16. Observations:

- ~42% of the extra tokens map to a burst of requests from a user-agent string 'brightcart-worker/2.1.0' that all carry the same model routing header but different request IDs.
- Many of those requests are subsecond streaming/flush combos that look like client retries with the same payload (body hash matches for a subset).
- There's a pattern of repeat sequences starting at 2026-06-15T02:04:xxZ and repeating every ~4 seconds for ~12 minutes.

Hypothesis: client-side replay/worker misconfiguration causing duplicate streaming sessions. Possible contributing factor: timezone mismatch between their deployment and ephemeral job scheduler.

Action items I recommend:
- Offer a provisional credit for the duplicated tokens while they validate config.
- Provide them a CSV mapping request_id -> timestamp -> token_count (we can redact IPs).
- Ask for a list of internal job IDs from BrightCart that correlate to 2026-06-15 02:00-02:30 UTC.

I can assemble the CSV excerpt (redwood_token_log_excerpt_0615.txt) and a short summary. If you want I can draft a credit note for finance.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

> On Thu, 18 Jun 2026 at 15:03, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > (internal reply quoted)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lee <anna.lee@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected jump on June invoice (INV-20260615)

Anna — quick update following our analysis. Thanks for the sample and the quick call earlier. Summary below (TL;DR at top).

TL;DR: We identified duplicated requests that account for ~36% of the reported overage. We are issuing a one-time provisional credit for the duplicated token usage while BrightCart confirms whether the duplicates originated from client retries. We will provide the CSV export and a short reconciliation memo for your finance team (including VAT treatment).

Details:
- Evidence: Attached redwood_token_log_excerpt_0615.txt (an excerpt) and the CSV mapping (brightcart_usage_sample_20260615.csv) showing matching body-hashes and repeated request IDs within the 02:04–02:16 UTC window.
- Root cause hypothesis: client-side worker retry loop (brightcart-worker/2.1.0) producing duplicate streaming sessions. Our server logs show identical payload hashes for many of the duplicated requests. We did not run any automatic replays from our side.
- Proposed commercial remediation: one-time credit of EUR 12,450 applied to INV-20260615 representing the duplicated tokens. This credit is provisional and contingent on BrightCart confirming their internal job IDs for that window or demonstrating the issue was accidental.
- VAT: Because BrightCart is EU-registered, Marissa will coordinate the VAT documentation and provide an updated credit note showing the VAT reclassification.

Next steps:
1) BrightCart to confirm whether they ran any scheduled jobs during 2026-06-15 02:00-02:20 UTC or can supply job IDs.
2) Once BrightCart confirms, Redwood will finalize the credit and update the invoice with VAT adjustments.
3) We will schedule a short post-mortem call to review retry/backoff recommendations.

Attachments: redwood_token_log_excerpt_0615.txt (log excerpt), brightcart_usage_sample_20260615.csv (their sample echoed back), INV-20260615-BrightCart.pdf (original invoice with provisional credit line added).

If you'd like the credit applied as a standalone refund instead of invoice adjustment let me know — we can handle both.

Best,
Evelyn
Account Lead, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

---
On Fri, 19 Jun 2026 at 08:24, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (internal diagnostic quoted)
From: Anna Lee <anna.lee@brightcart.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@brightcart.com
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 17:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unexpected jump on June invoice (INV-20260615)

Evelyn / Ben — thanks for the quick analysis and the provisional credit offer. We ran an internal check and confirmed a deployment of a new worker pool at 2026-06-15T02:02:00Z that did not implement the recommended idempotency token, so it looks like the duplicates were on our side.

We accept the provisional credit applied to INV-20260615. For procurement we need:
- A short reconciliation memo from Redwood (one page) that shows the duplicated token count and the credit amount (suitable for our AP team).
- Updated invoice PDF with the VAT line adjusted so our EU Finance team can close the month.
- A DocuSign link if Redwood prefers to formalize the credit note.

If you can send the memo and the updated invoice today that would be ideal. We'll schedule a 30-minute postmortem on Friday to review retry recommendations.

Thanks again,
Anna

Attachment: confirmation_from_brightcart_deploy.txt (note about worker pool deploy)
